name: Sauerkraut
subtitle: Salted cabbage prepared in a large batch
description: Firm cabbage is cut, salted, rested, heated, and cooled for a tangy salad or condiment. Use a current validated preservation procedure for any canning step.

instructions.text: Prepare the cabbage, discarding damaged portions while keeping the heads firm. Cut it into fine shreds and transfer to a large food-safe vessel.
Add the divided canning salt and mix thoroughly. Let the salted cabbage stand for 5 minutes, then work it until the cabbage softens and releases liquid.
Pack the cabbage and its liquid into the vessel, keeping it submerged. Hold at 75°F for the specified inactive period, following a validated fermentation procedure for food-safety details.

When the resting period is complete, prepare the sauerkraut for heating. Use a validated preservation procedure for jar preparation, filling, processing, and storage; those canning parameters are not specified here.
Bring the prepared sauerkraut and liquid to a simmer, then heat to boiling and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat, allow the batch to rest as directed by the validated preservation procedure, then cool promptly.
